title: Cross-presentation of caspase-cleaved apoptotic self-antigens in HIV infection
protocol: Isolate PBMCs and generate T cell clones as previously described.
Purify CD8+ T cells from PBMCs by positive selection with anti-CD8 mAb coupled to magnetic beads.
Derive immature DCs from peripheral monocytes purified by positive selection with anti-CD14 mAb coupled to magnetic beads.
Culture CD14+ cells for 7 days in RPMI 1640 medium containing specified supplements and cytokines.
Deplete B cells from PBMCs with anti-CD19 mAb coupled to magnetic beads.
Positively select CD1c+ DCs using biotin-labeled anti-CD1c mAb and anti-biotin mAb coupled to magnetic beads.
Obtain mature DCs by stimulating iDCs with CD40L-transfected J558L cells at a ratio of 1:1.
Stain the obtained DCs using anti-CD14, anti-CD86, anti-CD1a, anti-CD1c, anti-CD32, and anti-CD80 mAbs, as well as Annexin-V and propidium iodide.
Analyze stained cells using a FACSCanto flow cytometer with FACSDiva analysis software.
Plate cloned CD8+CD95+ T cells in a 24-well plate and incubate for 1 hour at 37°C.
Add 14 μg/ml caspase 3 inhibitor, C8I, or negative caspase control to the T cell clones.
Induce apoptosis of T cell clones by adding 500 ng/ml anti-Fas antibody for at least 6 hours.
Measure apoptosis by Annexin-V and PI staining followed by analysis by flow cytometry.
Purify apoptotic cells using Annexin V-conjugated magnetic microbeads.
Ensure the positively purified population consists of >99% Annexin V+ cells.
Use live cloned T cells promptly lysed by repeated freezing and thawing as control cells.

Measure spontaneous apoptosis of CD4+ T cells in fresh PBMCs from HIV-infected and healthy individuals before and after 18-h incubation at 37°C using Annexin-V, PI, and PE-Cy7-conjugated anti-CD4 mAb staining.
Use live cloned T cells lysed by repeated freezing and thawing as control for the measurement of spontaneous apoptosis.
Treat cloned CD8+CD95+ T cells with 14 μg/ml of caspase 3 inhibitor Z-DEVD-FMK, Z-IETD-FMK, or negative control K, Z-FA-FMK.
Dye the treated cells green with PKH27.
Induce the cells to undergo Fas-mediated apoptosis.
Co-culture apoptotic cells at a 1:1 ratio with iDCs.
Incubate the co-cultured cells either with rabbit anti-αvβ5 polyclonal antibody or control rabbit Ig, dyed red with PKH26.
Incubate the co-cultured cells for 12 h at 4°C and then at 37°C.
Analyze phagocytosis by flow cytometry after 12 h of incubation at 37°C.
Collect apoptotic and control cells.
Wash collected cells twice with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Centrifuge the washed cells at 1600 rpm for 10 min.
Dissolve the resulting pellets in 300 μl of two-dimensional sample buffer.
Rehydrate the sample into 11-cm nonlinear immobilized pH gradient strips.
Perform active sample rehydration into IPG strips at 50 V overnight.
Focus the samples in a Bio-Rad Protean Isoelectric Point Focusing Cell at 500 V for 30 min.
Increase voltage to 1000 V and focus for an additional 30 min.
Further increase voltage to 2000 V and focus for 15 min.
Continue focusing at 3000 V for 30 min.
Complete the focusing process at 5000 V for 7 hours.
Reduce the IPG strips with 2% w/v DTT in equilibration buffer for 10 minutes.
Alkalize the reduced IPG strips with 2.5% w/v iodoacetamide in equilibration buffer for 10 minutes.
Mount each IPG strip on an SDS-PAGE gel containing 12% T and 2.5% C acrylamide/bis-acrylamide.
Overlay the mounted strip with a solution of 0.5% w/v agarose and 0.5 M Tris-HCl pH 8.8.
Electrophorese the SDS-PAGE gel at 15 mA/gel for 15 minutes, then continue at 30 mA/gel for 5 hours at 10°C.
Fix the two-dimensional gels with a solution of 50% ethanol and 2% phosphoric acid for 2 hours.
Wash fixed gels in deionized water for 30 minutes.
Transfer washed gels to a staining solution containing 34% methanol, 17% w/v ammonium sulfate, and 2% phosphoric acid.
Stain the gels with Coomassie Brilliant Blue G-250 at 0.06% w/v for 1 hour.
Excise each 2DE spot of interest from the stained gel.
In-gel digest the excised spots with trypsin as described.
Carry out MALDI-TOF-MS of tryptic protein hydrolysates.
Identify proteins from the peptide mass spectra using PeptIdent analysis software accessed via ExPASy.
Conduct searches in the Swiss-Prot database, allowing for up to one missed cleavage and considering methionine in the oxidized form and cysteine treated with iodoacetamide.
Transfer 2DE gels onto nitrocellulose membranes electrophoretically.
Stain the membranes with Ponceau S solution.
Cut out the spots of interest from the stained membranes.
Elute proteins derived from these spots using an electron-elution solution (50 mM Tris-Cl pH 9.5, 1% [v/v] Triton X-100, 2% [w/v] SDS).
Centrifuge at 5000 rpm for 5 min to separate supernatant from precipitated proteins.
Remove the supernatant after centrifugation and precipitate proteins with 25% trichloroacetic acid (TCA).
Wash resulting protein pellet twice with cold acetone.
Quantify protein content before conducting cross-presentation experiments.
Collect apoptotic cells, CI-treated apoptotic cells, and control cells.
Wash collected cells twice with PBS.
Centrifuge washed cells at 1600 rpm for 10 min.
Mix the resulting pellets in 50 μl of lysis buffer solution.
Quantify the protein contents.
Separate proteins by SDS-PAGE.
Transfer each gel to a nitrocellulose membrane.
Immunoblot the proteins for vimentin using a guinea pig polyclonal antibody.
Incubate with secondary HRP-conjugated donkey anti-guinea pig IgG antibody.
Perform chemiluminescent detection using SuperSignal West Pico Chemiluminescent substrate to visualize the resulting proteins.
Filter human r-vimentin by using a Centricon Vivaspin 500.
Add 1 ml of caspase 3 buffer to the Centricon tubes.
Centrifuge twice at 4000 rpm for 30 min.
Collect 100 μg of vimentin.
Incubate collected vimentin with 150 ng of caspase 3 for 1 h at 37°C.
Separate complete and digested vimentin proteins on the basis of molecular weight under SDS-PAGE conditions.
Stimulate highly purified CD8+ T cells (1 x 10^5) from PBMCs with different peptides (5 μg/ml per single peptide) and irradiated autologous CD8-depleted PBMCs, used as antigen-presenting cells.
Perform stimulation directly in 96-well ELISPOT nitrocellulose-backed plates coated with capture anti-IFN-γ mAb.
Reveal IFN-γ spot formation after 6 to 8 h at 37°C using the AID ELISPOT Reader.

Determine resting CD8+ T cell responses by counting IFN-γ spots formed by short-term CD8+ T-cell lines obtained after one or two rounds of in vitro stimulation with peptides and irradiated autologous CD8-depleted PBMCs.
Stain PBMCs with allophycocyanin-labeled-HLA-A*0201 pentamers.
Stain cells with APC-Cy7-labeled anti-CD8 mAb.
Stain cells with FITC-labeled perforin mAb.
Stain cells with PE-labeled granzyme B mAb.
Obtain negative controls by staining cells with an irrelevant isotype-matched mAb.
Analyze samples using a FACSCanto flow cytometer and FACSDiva analysis software.
Stimulate part of the pentamer/anti-CD8-stained PBMCs with peptide plus anti-CD28 mAb for 6 h at 37°C.
Add Brefeldin-A to the stimulated cells at the second hour.
Wash cells with Perm/Wash buffer and stain intracellularly with PE-labeled anti-IFN-γ mAb for 30 min at 4°C.
Fix and permeabilize cells using Cytofix/Cytoperm solution at 4°C for 20 min.
Analyze fixed and permeabilized cells by flow-cytometry.
In some experiments, perform pentamer staining after overnight stimulation with peptide to determine the degree of TCR down-regulation.

Pulse immature monocyte-derived DCs or myeloid DCs (3 x 10^4) as APCs, with increasing concentrations of CI-treated, caspase-treated, untreated, r-vimentin-loaded apoptotic cells, control lysed cells, soluble antigens, or peptides in the presence or absence of 80 mM lactacystin for 18 h.
Wash APCs and coculture them with antigen-specific CD8+ T cells (2-3 x 10^4).
Reveal IFN-γ spot formation after 6–8 h at 37°C by an ELISPOT assay.

Pulse iDCs with apoptotic or control cells derived from HLA-A2-Epstein-Barr virus-transformed B cells previously infected by either WT-VV or NS3Ag-expressing VV and then coculture them with NS31406-1415-specific CD8+ T cell clones.
After 6 to 8 h at 37°C, reveal IFN-γ spot formation by CD8+ T cells by ELISPOT assay.
Double-stain PBMCs from patients or healthy donors (HDs) with pentamers and anti-CD8 mAb.
Culture PBMC in the presence of soluble r-CD40L molecules with autologous iDCs that have been pulsed or not with apoptotic cloned T cells.
After 6–8 h, test PBMC for their capacity to produce IFN-γ by ICSS assay.
Synthesize the peptides.
Test the synthesized peptides for class I binding capacity.
Present the binding data as IC50 nanomolar values.
